original_question: For a finite group G, let χ1(G) denote the totality of the degrees of all irreducible complex characters of G with allowance for their multiplicities. Suppose that H is a finite group with χ1(H) = χ1(G). a) If G is an almost simple group, must H be isomorphic to G? b) If G is a quasisimple group, must H be isomorphic to G? This is true if G is a simple group(see 11.8(a) in Archive).
target_in_paper: Problem 21.59 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" of The Kourovka Notebook.
correct_elements: Your draft is essentially the exact official formulation of Problem 21.59. It correctly uses the invariant χ1(G), correctly says that multiplicities of irreducible complex character degrees are retained, correctly assumes H is finite with χ1(H)=χ1(G), and correctly isolates the two cases asked in the paper: G almost simple and G quasisimple. It also correctly preserves the paper’s note that the simple-group case is already known.
missing_details: For a fully stand-alone version, χ1(X) should be written explicitly as a multiset, for example χ1(X) = {χ(1) : χ ∈ Irr(X)} with multiplicities.
The phrase "degrees of irreducible complex characters" can be sharpened by saying these are the values χ(1) for χ ∈ Irr(X).
If the question is to be self-contained for a reader outside the immediate paper context, the standard meanings of "almost simple" and "quasisimple" should be spelled out.
It helps to state explicitly that no further hypothesis on H is assumed beyond finiteness and χ1(H)=χ1(G).
refined_question: Let G and H be finite groups, and for any finite group X define χ1(X) to be the multiset {χ(1) : χ ∈ Irr(X)} of degrees of the irreducible complex characters of X, counted with multiplicity. Assume that χ1(H) = χ1(G). Must H be isomorphic to G in each of the following cases: (i) G is almost simple, that is, S ≤ G ≤ Aut(S) for some nonabelian finite simple group S; (ii) G is quasisimple, that is, G is perfect and G/Z(G) is a nonabelian finite simple group? The corresponding statement is known when G itself is simple.
justification: The exact match is Problem 21.59, whose wording is essentially identical to your draft. The problem is specifically about recognition of almost simple and quasisimple groups from the multiset of irreducible complex character degrees with multiplicities, and it explicitly notes that the simple-group case is already known. A nearby but different problem in the same paper, 21.135, asks only whether trivial solvable radical is preserved under equality of χ1; that is broader in one direction and weaker in conclusion, so it should not replace 21.59. The only real refinements needed are to make χ1 explicitly a multiset and to define almost simple/quasisimple so the question is fully stand-alone.
